text:
mia: Hey team — I opened a docs PR to update the Function/Tool calling guide + structured output section. Main changes: stricter JSON Schema examples, parsing patterns for nested objects, and SDK snippets for python/js. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482 :link:

alex: Thanks — quick skim. Looks good overall. Couple of questions: 1) are we changing the recommended response shape? 2) do we need a migration note for existing users relying on loose parsing?

mia: Good q. 1) We recommend the "response.schema" shape (see example) — it's stricter but backwards-compatible if you use a permissive parser. 2) Yes, added a short migration section called "Stricter schema opt-in" with examples for tolerant parsing.

sam: Can you paste the example SDK call here? Want to ensure the fetch/stream snippets match our latest client methods.

mia: Sure — Python example in the PR: 

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.chat.predict(
    model="gpt-structured-v1",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Create a JSON output with name, items[]"}],
    output_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type":"string"}, "items": {"type":"array"}}}
)
parsed = resp.get_structured()  # returns dict or raises SchemaValidationError
```

mia: JavaScript snippet also in PR, uses client.chat.stream for streaming and schema.validate(), added a tiny polyfill example for older runtimes.

zara: A couple editorial things: 1) Add a short rationale for stricter schema (reduce parsing errors, support auto-fill in downstream apps). 2) Move the guardrails section up near the top so customers see it first.

alex: On guardrails: can we add a short note about failing gracefully? Example: fall back to plain text if schema validation fails, and include telemetry hooks.

mia: Yup, added fallback code snippet and a suggested telemetry event name: "structured_output.validation_failed".

sam: Small nit — in the JS streaming example we still call oldClient.streamOnData. I updated it to client.chat.on_partial in the PR comments.

mia: Thanks, fixed. Also fixed a broken anchor link (was pointing to /docs/guides/old-json).

docs-bot: build/docs-staging — succeeded for PR 482 :white_check_mark:

alex: Can someone add an explicit example for nested objects + arrays? I think customers trip on that a lot.

mia: Added a "shopping list" nested example and a parsing pattern section showing how to walk nested arrays safely.

zara: Also add a short migration snippet for existing customers that want to keep permissive parsing: show how to call client.chat.predict(..., schema_mode="permissive") and then run a post-parse normalization.

mia: Done. I left a TODO for ops to check telemetry naming.

sam: LGTM from SDK side after the on_partial rename and a tiny formatting fix in the JS code block.

alex: I left two copy edits inline. Once those are done I can approve.

mia: Addressed both. Pushed one more commit.

zara: :thumbsup: When this merges can we add an entry to the migration changelog (release notes)?

mia: Yep — will add a short bullet under v1.7.0 notes.

alex: Approving now.

sam: Approved.

docs-bot: PR 482 merged into main by mia — changelog updated.

mia: Thanks everyone! I'll follow up with a short tweet + community post calling out the structured output improvements and migration tips.

zara: Great, thanks.

alex: One last follow-up: can we add an automated lint step to catch broken anchor links in docs? I opened an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/215

mia: Added to backlog. Closing thread.
